items.answer: is reflected back along the same path

items.stem: Which image is formed by a concave mirror with an object at F?
items.answer: a highly magnified image at infinity
items.markingKey: (a) A highly magnified image at infinity is the image formed by a concave mirror with an object at F. The others: a real, inverted image smaller than the object, between F and C – formed by a concave mirror with an object beyond C; a real, inverted image of the same size, at C – formed by a concave mirror with an object at C; a virtual, erect, magnified image behind the mirror – formed by a concave mirror with an object between P and F.
options: a highly magnified image at infinity
a real, inverted image of the same size, at C
a virtual, erect, magnified image behind the mirror
a real, inverted image smaller than the object, between F and C

items.stem: Why do dentists use concave mirrors?
items.answer: When the tooth is between P and F, a concave mirror forms an erect, magnified image, making it easy to see.

items.answer: A concave mirror: a solar furnace. A convex mirror: a rear-view mirror in a car.

items.stem: You are given a concave mirror and a convex mirror of the same size. Which will you use as a reflector in a car headlight and which as a side-view mirror? Justify.
items.answer: Concave mirror for the headlight (bulb at F gives a parallel beam); convex mirror as side-view mirror (erect, diminished image, wide field of view).

items.stem: Why do we use a sign convention in mirror formula problems?
items.answer: So that a single formula works for all cases, and the signs tell us the position (in front/behind) and nature of the image.

items.stem: An object is placed 25 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 25 cm. Where is the image formed?
An object is placed 48 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. Where is the image formed?
An object 4 cm high is placed 60 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. Find the position, nature and size of the image.
items.answer: v = +20 cm (behind the mirror); virtual, erect, diminished; height +1.33 cm (m = 0.333)
items.markingKey: f = +30 cm, u = −60 cm. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u ⇒ v = +20 cm. m = −v/u = 0.333; h′ = m × h = 1.33 cm. (1 mark v, 1 mark m, 1 mark nature)

items.stem: A convex mirror produces an image of magnification 0.4 of an object 10 cm high placed 15 cm in front of it. Find the height and position of the image and state its nature.
items.answer: h′ = 4 cm; v = +6 cm; virtual, erect, diminished
items.markingKey: h′ = m × h = 4 cm. m = −v/u ⇒ v = −m × u = +6 cm.

items.stem: An object 5 cm tall is placed 12 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 12 cm. (a) Using the mirror formula, find the position of the image. (b) Find its size and magnification. (c) State its nature. (d) Describe the ray diagram you would draw. (e) Give one use of this type of mirror.
items.answer: (a) v = +6 cm. (b) m = 0.5; h′ = 2.5 cm. (c) Virtual, erect, diminished. (d) A ray parallel to the axis reflects through (or appears to come from) F; a ray towards the centre of curvature C reflects back along itself; the image is where they meet (behind the mirror). (e) Rear-view mirrors in vehicles (wider field of view).

items.stem: What is meant by lateral displacement?
items.answer: The perpendicular shift of the emergent ray from the direction of the incident ray when light passes through a glass slab
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Lateral displacement – the perpendicular shift of the emergent ray from the direction of the incident ray when light passes through a glass slab.

items.stem: The refractive index of ice is 1.31. Find the speed of light in ice. (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
Why does the bottom of a tank of water appear raised?
items.answer: Light from the bottom bends away from the normal as it leaves water, so it seems to come from a point higher up.

items.answer: 1.08; dense flint glass is optically denser
items.markingKey: n = v(Canada balsam)/v(dense flint glass) = 1.08. The medium in which light is slower is denser.

items.stem: A ray of light enters a glass slab (n = 1.5) from air. Is the speed of light in glass more or less? Find it, and explain why the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray.
items.answer: Less: v = 3 × 10⁸/1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m/s. The bending towards the normal at the first face and away at the second are equal and opposite.
items.markingKey: 1 mark less. 1 mark speed. 1 mark parallel.

items.stem: In which of these media does light travel fastest? kerosene (n = 1.44), Canada balsam (n = 1.53), diamond (n = 2.42), benzene (n = 1.5)

items.stem: What is meant by the optical centre?
items.answer: The central point of a lens through which a ray passes without deviation
